Rashi on Ketubot 70a:10:1.hebrew: שלא תתקשט באחד מכל המינין - קונם בושם פלוני עלי, והוא קיים לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:10:1.english: Not to adorn herself with any one of all the kinds [of perfume] - [She vowed:] "Such-and-such perfume is konam [forbidden by vow] upon me," and he confirmed [the vow] for her.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:10:2.hebrew: בעניות שלא נתן קצבה - באשה עניה, אם לא נתן קצבה לדבר עד מתי אסרו עליה, הוא דיוציא ויתן כתובה; אבל אם נתן קצבה, תמתין עד אותו זמן. ובגמרא מפרש עד כמה היא קצבתה:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:10:2.english: For poor women, when he did not set a time limit - In [the case of] a poor woman, if he did not set a limit to the matter [specifying] until when he forbade it to her, [then] it is [in that case] that he must divorce [her] and give [her] [her] marriage contract; but if he set a time limit, she must wait until that time. And in the Gemara, it explains how long her time limit is.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:10:3.english: And for wealthy [women] - For they are accustomed to this.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:10:4.hebrew: עד שלשים יום - אם לא הדירה יותר, אין כופין להוציא:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:10:4.english: Up to thirty days - If he did not prohibit her by a vow [for] more [than thirty days], we do not compel [him] to divorce [her].

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:11:1.english: And since he is obligated to her - For [her] sustenance.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:1:1.hebrew: רבי מאיר - דמתני' היא, דאמר יעשה שליש מה שהושלש בידו:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:1:1.english: Rabbi Meir - [it] is [the ruling] of the Mishnah, as he says: "The third party shall do what was entrusted in his hand."

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:2:1.english: It is pleasing to him - that they give them all their needs.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:2:2.english: To urge them - That they should seek after their sustenance and that they should not be gluttons.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:3:1.hebrew: הפעוטות - תינוקות בני תשע ושמונה, כדאמרי' בהניזקין:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:3:1.english: The children - Young children, nine or eight [years old], as we say in [the chapter entitled] HaNizakin.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:3:2.hebrew: במטלטלי - דווקא, אבל במקרקעי לא, עד שיביאו שתי שערות או עד שיהא בן עשרים:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:3:2.english: With movable property - Specifically [movable property], but with real estate, [it is] not [valid] until they grow two [pubic] hairs or until he is twenty [years old].

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:4:1.hebrew: אפוטרופוס - שמינהו אבי יתומים או ב"ד:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:4:1.english: A steward [apotropos] - [One] whom the father of the orphans or the court appointed.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:5:1.english: From [the fact] that it teaches - In the Mishnah.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:5:2.hebrew: שאני הכא דאיכא שליש - שנשתלש לכך ופירשו לו מה יעשה בהן. אבל אפוטרופוס אינו אלא לעשות צורכי יתומים לכל הצריך, והרי אם מכרו אלו הפעוטות, אין זה שינוי מצות המת, שאף האפוטרופוס ימכור לצורך מזונותיהם:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:5:2.english: Here it is different, as there is a third party - For he was appointed as a trustee for this [purpose], and they specified to him what he should do with them. However, a guardian is only [appointed] to attend to the needs of the orphans for whatever is necessary, and behold, if these young children sold [property], this is not a deviation from the directive of the deceased, for the guardian too would sell [property] for their sustenance.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:5:3.hebrew: אם כן - דשליש דווקא, וטעמא לפי שפירשו לו לקנות שדה, ליתני יעשה שליש כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:5:3.english: If so - [that it is] specifically [because of the] third party, and the reason is because they specified to him to buy a field, let it teach: "the third party should execute," etc.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:5:4.hebrew: דאפילו בעלמא - במקום אפוטרופוס, דדמי קצת לשליש:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:5:4.english: That even generally - [i.e.,] where there is a guardian, which somewhat resembles a third party.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:7:1.hebrew: המדיר את אשתו מליהנות לו - אין הנאת תשמישו נאסר עליה, דהא משועבד לה. הלכך, בשביל תשמיש אין לנו לכופו להוציא וליתן כתובה. והנאת מזונות — בגמרא פריך: והא משועבד לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:7:1.english: One who vows [prohibiting] his wife from benefiting from him - The benefit of marital relations with him is not forbidden to her, for he is obligated to her [for it]. Therefore, on account of marital relations, we do not need to compel him to divorce [her] and pay [her] marriage contract. And [as for] the benefit of sustenance — in the Gemara it asks: "But is he not obligated to her?"

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:7:2.english: He must appoint a trustee [parnas] - An agent who will support her.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:8:1.hebrew: בישראל - אם ישראל הוא, שיכול להחזיר את גרושתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:8:1.english: In [the case of] an Israelite - If he is an Israelite, who can take back his divorcée.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:8:2.hebrew: ובכהן - שאם יגרשנה לא יוכל להחזירה, ושמא סופו יתחרט, יהבו ליה רבנן זימנא טפי:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:8:2.english: And [regarding] a priest - For if he divorces her, he will not be able to take her back, and perhaps in the end he will regret [it]; [therefore] the Sages gave him more time.

Rashi on Ketubot 70a:9:1.hebrew: אחד מכל הפירות - קונם פרי פלוני עלי, והוא קיים לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 70a:9:1.english: One of all the fruits - [She vowed,] "Konam [is] such-and-such a fruit upon me," and he upheld [it] for her.

Tosafot on Ketubot 70a:12:1.hebrew: הכא נמי כיון דמשועבד לה כו' - ואם תאמר: ולוקי כגון דתלינהו למזונותיה בתשמיש המטה, דאמר "יאסר תשמישך עלי אם אזונך"? וי"ל, דא"כ (אפי') שמואל דאמר לקמן "אפילו בסתם ימתין שמא ימצא פתח לנדרו", מ"מ לא הוה ליה למימר "יתר מיכן יוציא ויתן כתובה", אלא: לאחר שלשים תהנה ותאסר לבית הלל שבת אחת ולבית שמאי שתי שבתות; וכהאי גוונא פריך לקמן אמאי דמשני כגון דתלינהו לקישוטיה בתשמיש המטה. וליכא נמי למימר כגון דאמר "יאסר הנאת תשמישך עלי מעכשיו אם תהנה ממני", דאז אסורה ליהנות — דהא לרב יהודה דאמר בפרק שני דנדרים (דף יד:) "קונם עיני בשינה היום אם אישן למחר" שלא יישן היום פן יישן למחר, הכא נמי אסור לשמש שמא תהנה, דבתנאי לא מיזדהר איניש כדמפרש התם; ואפילו לרב נחמן דאמר התם מיזדהר, הכא מודה דאשה לא מיזדהרא כיון שלא נדרה. ובתוספות ה"ר יוסף, שפירש לפני רבינו שמואל מנוחתו כבוד, פירש דלקמן דווקא מוקי דתלינהו לקישוטיה בתשמיש המטה, דקתני "המדיר אשתו שלא תתקשט" ולא קתני "המדיר מקישוט" — משמע שפיר שמדירה מתשמיש מפני שלא תתקשט; אבל הכא דקתני "המדיר מליהנות", משמע שמהנאה ממש מדירה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70a:12:1.english: Here too, since he is obligated to her, etc. - And if you ask: Let [the Mishnah] establish [the case] as where he made her sustenance dependent on marital relations, such that he said, "May marital relations with you be forbidden to me if I feed you"? One can answer that if so, [even according to] Shmuel, who says later on, "Even in an unspecified [vow], he should wait [thirty days] lest he find an opening for his vow," nevertheless [the Mishnah] should not have said, "Beyond this, he must divorce [her] and give [her] the ketubah," rather [it should have said]: after thirty [days] she may derive benefit [from him] and she becomes forbidden [to him for] one week according to Beit Hillel and two weeks according to Beit Shammai; and in a similar manner [the Gemara] asks later on against that which it answers, "[It is a case] where he made her adornments dependent on marital relations." And one also cannot say [that the case is] where he said, "May the pleasure of marital relations with you be forbidden to me from now on if you derive benefit from me," so that then she is forbidden to derive benefit [from him] — for according to Rav Yehudah, who says in the second chapter of Nedarim (14b) [regarding one who says], "Konam [be] my eyes in sleep today if I sleep tomorrow," that he may not sleep today lest he sleep tomorrow, here too it would be forbidden [for him] to have marital relations [during the thirty days] lest she derive benefit [later], for a person is not careful about a condition, as [the Gemara] explains there; and even according to Rav Nachman, who says there [that] a person is careful, here he agrees that a woman is not careful since she did not make the vow. And in the Tosafot of Rabbi Yosef, who explained [this] before Rabbeinu Shmuel, may his rest be honor, he explained that specifically later on [the Gemara] establishes [the Mishnah] as where he made her adornments dependent on marital relations, because [the Mishnah] teaches, "One who vows against his wife that she not adorn herself," and does not teach, "One who vows [against her] from adornment" — [which] implies well that he is vowing her away from marital relations because she should not adorn herself; whereas here, where [the Mishnah] teaches, "One who vows [against his wife] from deriving benefit," it implies that he is vowing her away from actual benefit:

Tosafot on Ketubot 70a:2:1.hebrew: הא קיימא לן מצוה לקיים דברי המת - אפי' בבריא קיימא לן הכי, כדמוכח שילהי פ"ק דגיטין (דף טו.), דאמרינן: "רב אסי מוקי לה בבריא, והא קיימא לן מצוה לקיים דברי המת". יש מקשין: כיון דמצוה לקיים דברי המת, אם כן מאי אהני הא דדברי שכיב מרע ככתובים וכמסורין דמו? ואומר ר"ת דלא אמרי' מצוה לקיים דברי המת אלא כשהושלש מתחלה לכך; אי נמי, דווקא במת נותן בחיי מקבל, אבל דברי שכיב מרע בכל ענין כמסורין דמו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70a:2:1.english: "We maintain [that] it is a mitzvah to fulfill the words of the deceased" - Even regarding a healthy person we maintain this [law], as is proven at the end of the first chapter of Gittin (15a), where [the Gemara] says: "Rav Assi establishes it as referring to a healthy person, and [yet] we maintain [that] it is a mitzvah to fulfill the words of the deceased." Some ask: Since it is a mitzvah to fulfill the words of the deceased, if so, what does [the rule] that the words of a person on his deathbed are considered as written and as delivered accomplish? And Rabbeinu Tam says that we only say [it is] a mitzvah to fulfill the words of the deceased when [the gift] was deposited with a third party from the beginning for that purpose; alternatively, [it applies] specifically when the giver died during the lifetime of the recipient, whereas the words of a person on his deathbed are considered as delivered in every case.

Tosafot on Ketubot 70a:4:1.hebrew: אבל יש שם אפוטרופוס אין מקחן מקח - פי' ר"ח: דוקא מכר, אבל מתנתן מתנה, דלענין מתנה אין סברא לחלק בין יש שם אפוטרופוס לאין שם:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70a:4:1.english: "However, if there is a steward, their acquisitions are not acquisitions" - Rabbeinu Chananel explains: [This applies] specifically [to] a sale, but their gift is [a valid] gift, because with respect to a gift there is no reason to distinguish between [a case where] there is a steward and [a case where] there is not.

Tosafot on Ketubot 70a:7:1.hebrew: המדיר את אשתו מליהנות לו – פירש בקונטרס דאין הנאת תשמישו נאסר עליה, דהא משתעבד לה. משמע מתוך פירושו שיש בלשון זה איסור הנאת תשמיש. וקשה: דפריך בגמ' "וכיון דמשתעבד לה היכי מצי מדיר לה? והתנן קונם שאני עושה לפיך כו'" — מגופא דמתני' הו"מ למיפרך, דלא מצי אסר עליה תשמיש משום דמשועבד לה, דאם היה נאסר, יוציא ויתן כתובה, לב"ש בשתי שבתות ולב"ה שבת אחת. ועוד, כי מוקי לה בגמרא בהדירה כשהיא ארוסה, דאכתי לא משועבד לה, אם כן מתשמיש נמי חל הנדר, וליתני במתני' יוציא ויתן כתובה בשבת אחת לב"ה או בשתי שבתות לב"ש. ומפרש ר"ת ד"ליהנות לו" לא משמע אלא הנאת מזונות:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70a:7:1.english: "One who vows [to prohibit] his wife from benefiting from him" - Rashi explains that the benefit of his marital relations is not prohibited to her, because he is obligated to her. It is implied from his explanation that this expression includes a prohibition on the benefit of marital relations. And this is difficult: [regarding] what the Gemara asks, "Since he is obligated to her, how can he vow against her? Have we not learned in a Mishnah: 'Konam [that which] I produce for your mouth,' etc.?" — it could have asked from the Mishnah itself, that he cannot prohibit marital relations to her because he is obligated to her, for if it were prohibited, he would have to divorce [her] and pay the ketubah, according to Beit Shammai [after] two weeks and according to Beit Hillel [after] one week. And furthermore, when the Gemara establishes it [as referring to a case] where he made the vow when she was betrothed, when he is not yet obligated to her, if so, the vow takes effect on marital relations as well, and the Mishnah should have taught: he must divorce [her] and pay the ketubah after one week according to Beit Hillel or after two weeks according to Beit Shammai. Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explains that "from benefiting from him" implies only the benefit of sustenance.

Tosafot on Ketubot 70a:7:2.hebrew: יוציא ויתן כתובה – נראה לר"י דבכל הנך דקתני במתני' "יוציא" היינו שכופין אותו, דכיון דשלא כדין עביד כופין אותו להוציא, כדאשכחן בהחולץ (יבמות דף לט.) דתנן: "לא רצו חוזרין אצל גדול", ומפרש בגמרא: חוזרין אצל גדול למיכפייה הואיל ועליה מצוה רמיא. ועוד אמרי' לקמן (כתובות דף עז.): אמר רב: "האומר איני זן ואיני מפרנס — יוציא ויתן כתובה", ומסיק: "עד שכופין אותו להוציא יכפוהו לזון"; משמע דלשון "יוציא" — שכופין אותו להוציא. וליכא למימר דכפייה דהתם במילי ולא בשוטי: חדא, ד"בדברים לא יוסר עבד"; ועוד, מדפריך לעיל למ"ד מורדת ממלאכה: "והאמר רב האומר איני זן ואיני מפרנס יוציא ויתן כתובה" — ומאי קושיא? דלמא מתניתין דמוסיפין על כתובתה כשלא רצה להוציא! אבל אם כופין בשוטי — אתי שפיר. וא"ת א"כ, אמאי לא תני להו בהדי הנך שכופין להוציא (לקמן כתובות דף עז.)? וי"ל דלא תני במתני' אלא כגון מוכה שחין ובעל פוליפוס, דאתיין ממילא; אבל הנך דאתיא כפייה דידהו ע"י פשיעת הבעל — לא קתני. ומקמץ ומצרף ובורסי דקתני אפילו נעשו אחר שנשאו — ניחא, שאינם מתכוונים להקניט ולצער האשה. ועוד יש להביא ראיה ד"יוציא" משמע כפייה, מדאמר בסוף הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף סה: ושם): "עובדא הוה בבי כנישתא בקיסרי קמיה דר' יוחנן, ואמר: יוציא ויתן כתובה", ומשמע התם דכייפינן ליה. ותימה: אמאי לא חשיב לה לההיא ד"באה מחמת טענה" בהדי הנך שכופין להוציא, דהתם אינו פושע בה, דמה הוא יכול לעשות שהוא עקר? וי"ל משום דקתני סיפא: "בין שהיו עד שלא נשאו בין משנשאו", ולא שייך לומר "סבורה הייתי שאני יכולה לקבל", ורובייהו מיתרצי בהאי שינויא. ורבינו חננאל הביא מירושלמי דכל הנך "יוציא" דמתניתין — אין כופין. והכי איתא התם: "אמר שמואל: אין מעשין אלא לפסולות. אמר רבי שמואל: תנינא 'המדיר את אשתו מליהנות כו'' — שמענו שמוציא, שמענו שכופין?!" ופסק ר"ח משם: ש"מ שאין כופין אלא היכא שמפרש בהדיא "כופין"; אבל היכא דאמור רבנן "יוציא", אומרים לו: "כבר חייבוך חכמים להוציא, ואם לא תוציא מותר לקרותך עבריינא", אבל לכפותו — לא. ולקמן גבי "האומר איני זן ואיני מפרנס", לר"ח גרסינן בהדיא: "כופין אותו ויוציא ויתן כתובה". וההיא דהחולץ ד"חוזרין אצל גדול למיכפייה לכנוס או לפטור" — היינו לפי שמונע ממנה כל ענייני אישות, בין תשמיש המטה בין מזונות, אבל משום תשמיש המטה לחודיה או משום מזונות — לא. וההיא דסוף הבא על יבמתו — התם משמע דלכפותו אמר, דכשבא מעשה לפניו צוה להם להוציא. ויותר נראה דכופין בכל הני כדפירש ר"י, אלא דירושלמי קסבר ששייך כפייה במילי; אבל לדידן, דקיימא לן ד"בדברים לא יוסר עבד", ע"כ איירי בשוטי, כיון דלשון "יוציא" משמע כפייה היכא דעושה לה עולה. ומיהו אין לכוף שום אדם לגרש ולעשות מעשה עד שנמצא ראיה ברורה, דהא אמרינן דגט מעושה בישראל שלא כדין פסול, ואין להתיר אשת איש מספק:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70a:7:2.english: He must divorce [her] and give [her] the ketubah – It appears to R. Yitzchak [Ri] that in all those [cases] where the Mishnah teaches "he must divorce [her]," it means that we coerce him, for since he acts unlawfully, we coerce him to divorce [her], just as we find in [the chapter] HaCholetz (Yevamot 39a), where it was taught in the Mishnah: "If they did not want [to perform yibbum or chalitzah], they return to the elder [brother]," and the Gemara explains: "They return to the elder [brother] to coerce him, since the mitzvah rests upon him." And furthermore, we say later (Ketubot 77a): "Rav said: One who says, 'I will not feed and I will not support [my wife],' must divorce [her] and give [her] the ketubah," and [the Gemara] concludes: "Instead of coercing him to divorce [her], let them coerce him to feed [her]!" This implies that the expression "he must divorce [her]" [means] that we coerce him to divorce [her]. And one cannot say that the coercion there is with words and not with lashes: first, because "a servant will not be corrected by words"; and furthermore, because [the Gemara] challenges above the one who says [that a rebellious wife is one who] rebels against [household] work: "Did not Rav say: One who says, 'I will not feed and I will not support [my wife],' must divorce [her] and give [her] the ketubah?" Now what is the difficulty [if coercion were only with words]? Perhaps our Mishnah, which [rules that] we add to her ketubah, is when he did not want to divorce [her]! Rather, if we coerce [him] with lashes, it works out well. And if you ask: If so, why did [the Mishnah] not teach these alongside those [cases] where we coerce [him] to divorce [her] (below, Ketubot 77a)? One can answer that the Mishnah only taught [cases] such as one afflicted with boils or one who has a polyp, which come about on their own; however, these [cases], where their coercion comes about through the husband's negligence, it did not teach. And [as for] a gatherer [of dog excrement], a copper refiner, and a tanner, which [the Mishnah] teaches even [when] they became [so] after they married — that is fine, because they do not intend to provoke and distress the wife. And furthermore, one can bring a proof that "he must divorce [her]" implies coercion from what it says at the end of [the chapter] HaBa Al Yevimto (Yevamot 65b and there): "There was an incident in the synagogue in Caesarea before R. Yochanan, and he said: He must divorce [her] and give [her] the ketubah," and it is implied there that we coerce him. And it is astonishing: why did [the Mishnah] not count that [case] of [a woman who] comes with a claim [that she wants a child] alongside those where we coerce [him] to divorce [her], for there he is not negligent toward her, since what can he do that he is sterile? One can answer: because the latter clause teaches, "whether they existed before they married or after they married," and it is not applicable to say [regarding sterility], "I thought I could endure it" — and most of them are resolved by this answer. Now Rabbeinu Chananel cited from the Yerushalmi that [in] all these [cases of] "he must divorce [her]" in our Mishnah, we do not coerce. And thus it is stated there: "Shmuel said: We do not coerce [a husband to divorce] except for disqualified [marriages]. R. Shmuel said: We learned [in a Mishnah], 'One who vows his wife from benefiting, etc.' — we have heard that he must divorce [her]; have we heard that we coerce [him]?" And Rabbeinu Chananel ruled from there: Learn from this that we do not coerce except where [the Mishnah] explicitly states "we coerce"; however, where the Rabbis said "he must divorce [her]," we say to him, "The Sages have already obligated you to divorce [her], and if you do not divorce [her], it is permitted to call you a transgressor," but to coerce him — no. And later, regarding "One who says, 'I will not feed and I will not support,'" according to Rabbeinu Chananel we read explicitly: "We coerce him, and he must divorce [her] and give [her] the ketubah." And that [passage] in HaCholetz, that "they return to the elder [brother] to coerce him to marry [her] or to release [her]," is because he withholds from her all matters of marriage, both marital relations and sustenance; however, on account of marital relations alone or sustenance [alone] — no. And [as for] that [passage] at the end of HaBa Al Yevimto — there it implies that he said [it] to coerce him, for when the case came before him, he commanded them to divorce. Yet it appears more [likely] that we coerce in all of these, as Ri explained, except that the Yerushalmi holds that coercion with words is applicable; whereas according to us, since we hold that "a servant will not be corrected by words," perforce it speaks of lashes, since the expression "he must divorce [her]" implies coercion where he does her an injustice. Nevertheless, one should not coerce any man to divorce and take action until we find a clear proof, for we say that a bill of divorce coerced by Jews unlawfully is invalid, and we must not permit a married woman [to remarry] out of doubt.

Tosafot on Ketubot 70a:9:1.hebrew: שלא תטעום אחד מכל הפירות - לאו בכל פירות מדיר לה, דא"כ לא הוה חייל, דאי אפשר לה לקיים, כדאמרי' בריש פרק שני דנדרים (דף יד:) דכי אמר "קונם עיני בשינה" סתם, לא חייל נדר למיסר שינה; אלא שלא תטעום במין אחד שבפירות, כדאמרינן בתוספתא, דאפילו לא טעמה מין זה מעולם. אבל למאי דסלקא דעתין דאדרה איהו ותלנהו בתשמיש המטה — חל אפילו הדירה מכל פירות, כיון דאפשר לה לאכול וליאסר בתשמיש המטה, כי ההיא דשלהי נדרים (דף פט:) דאמר "תיתסר כל הנאות דעלמא עלי כו'", ושרקיה טינא שלא יהנה מן העולם — אלמא חל הנדר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 70a:9:1.english: "Not to taste one of all the fruits" - He does not vow against her [regarding] all fruits, for if so [the vow] would not take effect, since it is impossible for her to fulfill [it], as we say at the beginning of the second chapter of Nedarim (14b) that when one says, "My eyes are konam [forbidden] with respect to sleep," without specification, the vow does not take effect to forbid sleep. Rather, [it means] that she shall not taste one type of fruit, as we say in the Tosefta, that even if she had never tasted this type [it applies]. However, according to what we initially thought — that he vowed against her and made them contingent on marital relations — [the vow] takes effect even if he vowed against her [regarding] all fruits, since it is possible for her to eat and become forbidden in marital relations; like that [incident] at the end of Nedarim (89b) where [someone] said, "All pleasures of the world shall be forbidden to me," etc., and plastered [it] with clay so that he would not benefit from the world — thus [we see] the vow takes effect.
